newsitem.title: USA: Tanker accident shuts Portland, Maine Harbor.
newsitem.headline: Tanker accident shuts Portland, Maine Harbor.

text.p: An oil tanker carrying some 750,000 barrels of distillate fuel collided with a bridge near Portland Harbor Friday, shutting the port and causing an unspecified quantity of fuel to spill, the U.S. Coast Guard said.
The tanker, the Julie N., was leaking approximately 1,000 barrels an hour of number six residual fuel, the Coast Guard said.
The collision took place sometime earlier this afternoon, he added, but it was unclear what quantity of fuel had already spilled into the river.
"Apparently, a tanker struck a bridge," said Coast Guard spokesman Tim Panovec. "There is a containnment boom around the vessel, but it is still leaking oil at this time."
Maine environmental officials said both diesel fuel and residual fuel were involved in the spill, which occurred in the Fore River at the Portland-South Portland Bridge leading into the harbor.
"It was dead high tide, which means the oil spread out over a pretty wide area," said Deborah Garrett, spokeswoman for Maine's Department of Environmental Protection.
The bridge was also damaged in the collision, but it remained open to traffic, Coast Guard officials said.
There were no injuries reported in the accident.
